page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8488C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock of 3.2 GHz, the configuration supplies 4 burstable vCPUs across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). System memory consists of 8.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 RAM, delivering a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage and possessing a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-core performance alongside modest multi-core capacity reflecting its two physical cores and burstable allocation model. In compute evaluations, the instance reached a stress-ng single-core score of 2032.08 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1912.0, both falling within the middle 50% distribution. Multi-core throughput ranked in the lower 25% bracket, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 4231.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 4216.75. Memory performance showed mixed results, achieving 27.34 GB/sec in uncached large-block write bandwidth, while general PassMark memory tests placed in the bottom decile at 978.31.

The c7i-flex.xlarge trades sustained multi-threaded compute density and high baseline network throughput for cost-efficient burstable processing. With support for matrix acceleration instructions and balanced single-core metrics, this instance is suited for batch processing, web serving, microservices, light data parsing, and continuous integration tasks that experience intermittent processor demand.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine utilizing the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8488C x86_64 processor clocked at 3.2 GHz. The setup features 4 burstable vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 8.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, and 105 MB of L3 cache, complemented by AMX and AVX-512 acceleration sets. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs, operating with a baseline network speed of 1 Gbps. Benchmark profiles show reliable mid-tier single-core CPU throughput, including a 1912.0 Geekbench single-core score, alongside average performance in static web serving and large-block memory writes. However, its multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth sit in lower tiers due to the dual-core burstable layout. This hardware balance provides a cost-conscious compute profile suitable for intermittent web serving, build pipelines, and lightweight application tiers.
